title: Investcom launches Lebanon's first AMPS mobile service
why: Analogue mobile service predates the 1994 GSM licences. Sodetel gained a switching monopoly the same year.

title: Aoun leaves Beirut for exile in France
why: Conditional amnesty ended the 1990 stand-off; his exile lasted until 2005.

title: Horizon 2000 reconstruction programme targets about $20 billion
why: The state-led recovery plan behind later debt growth; real GDP rose 8% in 1994 and 7% in 1995.

title: Digital switching contract worth $430 million signed
why: Upgraded Lebanon's analogue telephone exchanges; it was tendered in 1993 and signed in March 1994.

title: Government orders dissolution of the Lebanese Forces
why: Geagea's deputy Fouad Malek was taken into custody; Geagea himself was arrested a month later.

title: Aoun founds the Free Patriotic Movement
why: Launched at a National Conference during his exile; later the largest Christian bloc.

title: Hariri government bans organised demonstrations
why: Enforced by the army; troops dispersed protests on 13 September 1994, as HRW later reported.

title: CADMOS submarine cable to Cyprus starts operating
why: A 230 km cable from Beirut and Jdeideh to Pentaskhinos; Lebanon's early international link.

title: About 30% of Lebanese below poverty line; 500,000 Syrian workers
why: Estimates cited for 1996, showing the social cost of the reconstruction decade.

title: Beirut Stock Exchange reopens with electronic trading
why: Closed since 1983; reopened with a system built with the Paris bourse.

title: BERYTAR submarine cable starts operating
why: Interlinked with CADMOS, it expanded Lebanon's international capacity before the I-ME-WE cable.

title: Israel announces conditional intent to implement Resolution 425
why: Israel declared it on 1 April 1998; full withdrawal came 24 May 2000, 22 years after the resolution.

title: Postal service privatised and handed to LibanPost
why: LibanPost was set up on 25 August 1998; the decision sparked controversy. Canadian partners later sold out in 2001.

title: South Lebanon Army starts dismantling its Jezzine headquarters
why: A first step in the collapse of the Israeli-backed militia a year before the withdrawal.

title: Israeli cabinet votes unanimously for full withdrawal by July
why: Set the timetable that ended with the pull-out of May 2000.

title: South Lebanon Army positions collapse as Hezbollah advances
why: The militia fell apart at the Israeli pull-out; its equipment largely passed to Hezbollah.

title: Hezbollah and Amal form joint electoral coalition
why: Cemented the Shia duo that has dominated southern lists since.

title: Five-year telecom rehabilitation plan published with $786 million budget
why: Aimed to rebuild and modernise the network before the 2002 liberalisation law.

title: Qornet Shehwan Gathering founded with Patriarch Sfeir's blessing
why: Twenty-nine figures formed an anti-Syria platform that fed the 2005 Independence Intifada.

title: US enacts Syria Accountability and Lebanese Sovereignty Restoration Act
why: Introduced 12 April 2003; targeted Syrian support for terrorism and its presence in Lebanon.

title: German-mediated prisoner swap frees Dirani and 22 Lebanese detainees
why: Israel released about 400 Palestinians and returned remains of 59 for businessman Tenenbaum and three bodies.

title: Cabinet approves decrees creating the TRA and Liban Telecom
why: Implemented Law 431/2002; Liban Telecom was meant to start privatising Ogero.

title: Hariri funeral becomes a mass display of anger at Syria
why: Opposition leaders blamed Damascus; a month later 1.2 to 1.5 million rallied on 14 March.

title: Assad announces pull-back of Syrian forces to the Bekaa
why: No timetable was given; complete withdrawal followed on 26 April 2005.

title: Aoun returns to Beirut after 15 years in exile
why: Returned after the Syrian withdrawal; his bloc later allied with Hezbollah.

title: Beirut airport renamed Rafic Hariri International Airport
why: Renamed four months after the assassination of the former prime minister.

title: Geagea walks free from prison after parliament's amnesty vote
why: Parliament voted the amnesty on 18 July 2005; he left Lebanon for medical care.

title: Oversubscribed $750 million Eurobond issue after the Hariri shock
why: Deposit inflows resumed in late 2005 and spreads narrowed by March 2006.

title: Army arrests alleged Israeli spy ring led by Mahmoud Rafeh
why: Reportedly confessed to the Majzoub killing; one of several espionage cases of the period.

title: About 800,000 attend Pierre Gemayel's funeral rally
why: Turned the funeral into a rally against Syria and its allies.

title: Remaining 17 ministers approve the Hariri tribunal
why: Taken after Shia ministers resigned; President Lahoud rejected it on 9 December.

title: Nearly one million join opposition protest downtown
why: Peak of the sit-in that began 1 December and ran until 2008.

title: Sunni-Shia student clashes at Beirut Arab University
why: Spread into wider unrest the day after the general strike.

title: TRA board finally appointed
why: Law 431 had created the regulator in 2002; it only started work five years later.

title: Lebanese army and Israeli forces trade fire near Avivim
why: The UN called it the first armed incident since the 2006 war; no injuries.

title: Unclaimed rockets fired from Lebanon into northern Israel
why: UN condemned it as a serious violation of the ceasefire; Hezbollah denied involvement.

title: Beirut Internet Exchange launched, first IXP in Lebanon
why: Lets ISPs exchange traffic locally instead of routing abroad.

title: UN report counts 69 dead and 180 wounded in May clashes
why: Gives the toll of the May 2008 fighting between Hezbollah and pro-government forces.

title: Assad and Sleiman agree in Paris to open embassies
why: Agreed at the Union for the Mediterranean summit; the first Syrian recognition of Lebanese sovereignty.

title: Syrian embassy opens in Beirut
why: First diplomatic mission after Syria's 2008 recognition; Lebanon opened its Damascus embassy in March 2009.

title: Beirut stock market ranked world's best performer by MSCI
why: Stock index rose 51% in 2008 while most markets fell, with growth at 8.5%.

title: Saad Hariri visits Damascus for three days
why: Marked a thaw between the Hariri camp and Assad four years after the assassination.

title: Dozens of Aoun supporters arrested for leaflets and demonstrations
why: Forty held in Kesrouan and 58 in Ashqout; Aoun's loyalists were policed hard after his surrender.

title: Cost-of-living protests erupt from Tyre to Zahle
why: Next day a four-day general strike followed; Prime Minister Karami resigned on 6 May.

title: Four-day general strike over the collapsing lira
why: Declared on 5 May with thousands mobilised in Beirut and the regions; it brought down the Karami cabinet.

title: Four ministers quit over Lahoud's term extension
why: Economy, culture, environment and a fourth minister resigned after the 3 September vote.

title: New conscription system cuts service to six months
why: Pledged to end compulsory service within two years; it ended on 10 February 2007.

title: Israel imposes air, land and sea blockade on Lebanon
why: Beirut airport was bombed and flights diverted to Cyprus; naval and air blockades lasted until 7-8 September.

title: Israeli warship INS Hanit hit by anti-ship missile off Beirut
why: Hezbollah declared open war the same day; its offices in Beirut were hit for the first time.

title: Hezbollah rockets hit Haifa, killing eight at a rail depot
why: Marked a deeper reach into northern Israel; Acre and Nahariya were also hit.

title: Israel drops 23 tons of explosives on Bourj al-Barajneh bunker
why: Targeted a suspected Hezbollah leadership bunker; Hezbollah said none of its members were hurt.

title: About 2,000 Israeli troops enter south Lebanon; Maroun al-Ras seized
why: Start of limited ground incursions in the 2006 war.

title: Battle for Bint Jbeil begins
why: Israeli forces met heavy resistance in the largest town near the border; they pulled out on 29 July.

title: Rocket strike at Kfar Giladi kills 12 Israeli reservists
why: Deadliest single strike on Israeli soldiers in the 2006 war.

title: Cabinet extends Siniora plan with 15,000 Lebanese troops for the south
why: Plan first presented in Rome on 27 July; it foreshadowed Resolution 1701's deployment.

title: Israel lifts naval blockade; war formally ends
why: Air blockade lifted 7 September; ceasefire had held since 14 August.

title: Compulsory military service ends in Lebanon
why: Ended under the 2005 conscription reform, two years after it was announced.

title: Law lets Lebanese abroad vote from 2013
why: Passed in 2008 to let expatriates vote in Lebanese elections beginning in 2013.

title: Caretaker labour minister signs decree on Palestinian work rights
why: Decree by Boutros Harb carried out the August 2010 amendments to labour law.

title: Parliament passes law to restore citizenship to people of Lebanese origin
why: Part of a batch of laws; Bassil began implementing it on 5 May 2016.

title: Army builds concrete wall around Ain al-Hilweh camp
why: Authorities began the wall and watch towers around the largest Palestinian camp in 2016.

title: DiasporaID programme launched to link Lebanese abroad
why: Launched August 2017; Aoun urged diaspora children to take Lebanese citizenship on 8 August.

title: Aoun signs naturalisation decree for about 300 people
why: Reported number of individuals; criticised as the first such decree in years under an anti-naturalisation president.

title: Riot police fire tear gas and rubber bullets at anti-corruption protesters
why: More than 30 activists were arrested and released within days; protests near parliament continued.

title: Minimum wage raised 40% to LBP 700,000 after strike threats
why: Raised from LBP 500,000; most unions struck anyway, except the general workers' union.

title: Lebanon accedes to CEDAW
why: Acceded in 1997; the National Commission for Lebanese Women followed in 1998.

title: National Commission for Lebanese Women established
why: State body for women's policy created a year after CEDAW accession.

title: Mutiny at Roumieh prison: inmates hold five guards hostage
why: An early sign of the overcrowding and control problems in Lebanon's main prison.

title: Former minister Michel Samaha arrested over explosives plot
why: Alleged transport of explosives from Syria; he was convicted in 2015 and freed in August 2022.

title: US designates Michel Samaha a global terrorist
why: Washington named him for helping Damascus launch attacks in Lebanon.

title: Security forces storm Islamist wing of Roumieh prison
why: Clashes followed in the building housing Islamist inmates.

title: Saudi Arabia halts $3 billion package to the Lebanese army
why: Riyadh cited Lebanon's failure to condemn attacks on its missions in Iran.

title: Samaha sentenced to 13 years with hard labour
why: A second sentence for planning terrorist acts, after a 2015 conviction.

title: Saudi Arabia bans Lebanese fruit and vegetable imports
why: Followed a captagon seizure of 5.3 million pills hidden in pomegranates.

title: Minister Kordahi resigns in a bid to end the Gulf crisis
why: Resigned after Saudi Arabia expelled Lebanon's ambassador on 29 October over his remarks on Yemen.

title: Michel Samaha released after ten years in prison
why: He was arrested in August 2012 over the explosives plot.

title: Kafalat loan-guarantee company set up for small businesses
why: Created by the deposit guarantee institute and commercial banks; BDL subsidised its interest.

title: BDL issues Basic Circular 69 on electronic banking
why: First regulatory framework for e-banking; amended repeatedly, notably in 2013 and 2016.

title: BDL issues Basic Circular 83 on money laundering and terror financing
why: Core AML framework for banks, later amended in 2013 and 2016.

title: BDL launches about $1.46 billion stimulus package of cheap bank credit
why: Packages continued each year to 2018, totalling over $6 billion; housing loans took the largest share.

title: Prime Minister Diab announces first sovereign default
why: Announced two days before the $1.2bn Eurobond fell due on 9 March 2020.

title: Black-market dollar hits LBP 6,075
why: Pound had lost 75% against the dollar on the parallel market since 2019.

title: Judge freezes some of Riad Salameh's assets
why: Followed a complaint by lawyers in July 2020; Judge Faisal Makki ordered a protective freeze.

title: OCCRP reports Salameh-linked offshore assets of nearly $100 million
why: Overseas holdings, mostly UK property, were reported in August 2020; he denied wrongdoing.

title: BDL Circular 152 offers interest-free dollar repair loans after port blast
why: Issued two days after the explosion; banks were to lend to homes and firms, refinanced by BDL.

title: BDL Circular 153 lets students abroad transfer $10,000 at official rate
why: Excluded recent students; Law 193 of October 2020 followed.

title: Parliament passes Law 193, the student dollar law
why: Obliges banks to transfer student funds at the official rate; BDL implemented it with Circular 155 on 9 December 2020.

title: Pound hits LBP 10,000 to the dollar
why: Record low at the time; it kept falling through 2021.

title: World Bank warns crisis may be among three worst since 1850s
why: Said the system 'benefited a few for so long'; later reports called it a deliberate depression.

title: Judge Ghada Aoun subpoenas Salameh after he skips questioning
why: A raid on his office and homes followed; his home was raided again on 21 June 2022.

title: Security forces raid Salameh's home again
why: Second raid, part of the illicit enrichment investigation of the central bank governor.

title: IMF lowers Lebanon growth forecast to 2%
why: Second report of 2015 cut it from 2.5%; Syria-war spillover weighed on growth.

title: Israeli air raids hit Beirut power stations and bridges
why: Heaviest raids in three years followed Hezbollah rocket fire; at least eight to nine civilians died and Beirut lost power.

title: Villagers storm Khiam prison and free about 130 detainees
why: Amnesty counted 144 freed; the SLA-run centre had held people without trial for up to 15 years.

title: Law 220 on the rights of persons with disabilities
why: Parliament's record dates it 29 May 2000; Gazette publication followed in June. Quotas on jobs, transport and housing.

title: Army deploys in Jabal Mohsen and Bab al-Tabbaneh under Tripoli security plan
why: At least 30 had died in March fighting; troops removed barricades and cut local 3G the next day.

title: Public employees and teachers hold general strike for salary scale
why: Parliament committees failed on 4 April to agree funding for the raise; the UCC threatened an open-ended strike.

title: UCC announces open-ended strike and exam-correction boycott from 7 June
why: Part of the 2012 to 2017 fight over a new public-sector pay scale.

title: Education minister grants passing certificates after teachers boycott exam marking
why: Official exams went unmarked because of the pay-scale dispute; the UCC vowed to sue over the certificates.

title: UCC general strike across ministries and municipalities
why: Aimed at forcing parliament to pass the pay scale despite the presidential vacuum.

title: Parliament passes Law 105 on the missing and forcibly disappeared
why: Creates a National Commission to clarify the fate of those missing since the civil war.

title: Qabr Shamoun incident: two bodyguards of Minister Saleh al-Gharib killed
why: Convoy came under fire in a Druze area near Aley; PSP and Gharib's side gave rival accounts.

title: Hezbollah brings Iranian fuel into Lebanon via Syria
why: Trucks crossed at al-Ain; opponents warned of US sanctions; the state still had no fuel plan.

title: 67,884 Lebanese travellers and emigrants leave in one year
why: Second-highest annual outflow of 1992 to 2022, per Information International's Interior Ministry-based count.

title: Government policy statement limits entry of Syrians
why: Denied entry to Syrians from areas not adjacent to Lebanon and moved to review refugee status.

title: Border restrictions on Syrians start in north, reach Masnaa by September
why: Imposed after the Arsal clashes; new UNHCR registrations had run at about 10,000 a week.

title: Cabinet adopts policy to reduce the number of Syrian refugees
why: First comprehensive policy: stop entries bar humanitarian cases, encourage return, tighten security and work rules.

title: 18,863 Lebanese emigrate in 2017, per Information International
why: Figure for 2017; the series rose to 33,129 in 2018 and 66,806 in 2019.

title: 33,129 Lebanese emigrate in 2018
why: Rising before the 2019 crisis; the 2017 to 2021 total reached 215,653.

title: 66,806 Lebanese emigrate in 2019
why: Peak before the pandemic dip; the revolt and collapse drove the jump.

title: Emigration falls to 17,721 as COVID closes borders
why: A pause between the 2019 and 2021 waves; the port blast later triggered a surge.

title: Lebanon holds first Arab gay pride week; opening event cancelled
why: Opening event was cancelled over threats of violence; NBC called it the first Arab pride week. (corrected from 2017-05-21; Pride week ran 14-21 May 2017, opening event on the first Sunday; old Reuters link covered the 2018 edition)

title: Beirut Pride organiser detained overnight; events cancelled
why: Hadi Damien was held at Hbeish police station and pressed to sign a pledge; the prosecutor's ban stopped the week.

title: 42,199 leave Lebanon in first ten months of 2022
why: Against 65,172 over the same period of 2021; totals since 1992 reached 815,410.

title: Hezbollah and Amal ambush Israeli naval commandos at Ansariya
why: Twelve Israeli soldiers died; the worst Israeli loss in Lebanon since 1985 fed the debate on withdrawal.

title: Hariri cabinet approves reform package to appease protesters
why: Halved ministers' pay and passed a 2020 budget with no new taxes; protesters rejected it and demanded the government go.

title: Report finds startup investment down over 70% since 2017
why: KAS and Arabnet found 54.3% of startups moved part of operations abroad; deals fell from 56 to 12.

title: Circular 331 de facto frozen as BDL blocks startups from relocating
why: Lollar capital calls and devaluation stalled venture funds that had put about $400 million into start-ups.

title: Government approves master plan to rebuild Beirut Central District
why: Approved in March 1994; Solidere was formed on 5 May 1994 to carry it out.

title: Interest payments take about 68% of the budget deficit
why: Showed the debt burden building during the reconstruction years.

title: Unemployment about 14%, 29% among 15-24 year olds
why: Zero growth in 2000 as the post-war recovery stalled.

title: Reserves fall $2.4bn in 2000 and $1.6bn in first half of 2001
why: Reserves drained during the early 2000s slowdown; the VAT followed in 2002 and Paris II in November 2002.

title: Ericsson lays about 2,000 km of fibre backbone
why: Built the high-speed backbone alongside the first metropolitan Ethernet network.

title: Hariri family announces Saad will lead the Future Movement
why: Two months after Rafic Hariri's assassination; Saad later led the March 14 Alliance.

title: Geagea returns to Lebanon after post-release medical stay
why: Back on his birthday; he settled in the Cedars region, later in Maarab.

title: Siniora presents seven-point plan at Rome conference
why: Plan to end the war; on 7 August it was extended to include 15,000 Lebanese soldiers in the south.

title: MTN buys Investcom for $5.5 billion
why: Lebanese Mikati-family telecom group sold to South Africa's MTN.

title: Solidere deploys broadband network with Orange Business Services
why: Downtown Beirut gets a private fibre network, years before nationwide fibre.

title: Geagea issues historic apology at Jounieh rally
why: Public apology before thousands of supporters for wartime acts, part of Christian reconciliation.

title: Public debt reaches 150.7% of GDP
why: Fourth highest in the world by ratio, down from 154.8% in 2009.

title: Nationwide internet blackouts after unannounced I-ME-WE cable maintenance
why: Exposed Lebanon's dependence on a single subsea cable and Ogero's lack of notice.

title: Ministry signs MoU with CYTA on EUROPA cable to Cyprus
why: Planned to replace the aging CADMOS cable; still pending in 2019.

title: Unemployment reaches 20%, doubled in three years
why: Syrian war spillover hit trade, tourism and investment.

title: Saad Hariri returns to Lebanon after three years abroad
why: He had lived in Paris since 2011; he became prime minister again in December 2016.

title: Telecom ministry launches five-year 2020 Digital Telecom Vision
why: Plan under Minister Boutros Harb; by April 2015 only one fibre sub-ring had been switched on.

title: Hezbollah ends silence and backs Aoun for president
why: Opened the way to Aoun's election in October 2016.

title: Saad Hariri declares support for Aoun's presidency
why: Broke the 29-month presidential vacuum 11 days later when Aoun was elected.

title: Aoun signs Lebanon's first animal protection law
why: Protects domestic and wild animals from abuse.

title: Protester Hussein al-Attar shot dead during demonstrations
why: One of the first deaths of the 17 October movement.

title: Protester Alaa Abou Fakhr shot dead at Khalde roadblock
why: A soldier was charged on 21 November in the killing.

title: First civil parade on Independence Day in Martyrs' Square
why: Civil society staged the 76th independence celebrations instead of the state.

title: About a thousand march in Beirut against sexual harassment
why: Women-led march during the protest movement; harassment law passed a year later.

title: Mass protests resume after weeks of relative calm
why: Revived the 17 October movement as the economy worsened.

title: Protesters mark Lebanon's centenary with port-blast justice demands
why: Greater Lebanon was proclaimed on 1 September 1920.

title: Government asks a private individual to keep managing the .lb domain
why: A temporary arrangement for the country domain, registered in 1993, that government sites rely on.

title: Aoun tells Hariri to form a government or make way
why: Cabinet talks had stalled for five months; Hariri quit on 15 July 2021.

title: Speedtest ranks Lebanon 160th for broadband
why: Also 82nd for mobile; shows the decay of the network before the telecom collapse.

title: About 2,800 Amal fighters join the Lebanese army
why: Part of folding militias into state forces after the war; Hezbollah kept its arms.

title: Anti-Syria demonstration turns violent; hundreds arrested
why: Security forces repressed the protest of Aounists and others, a prelude to the 2005 Independence Intifada.

title: Assad says troops will leave Lebanon in the next few months
why: No timetable was given; Syrian troops completed their exit in late April 2005.

title: Army takes Nahr al-Bared camp, ending 15-week battle with Fatah al-Islam
why: About 155 soldiers died in over three months of heavy fighting.

title: Government cancels two Hezbollah-related decisions, ending the fighting
why: Cancelled on President Suleiman's proposal; the Doha talks followed from 17 May.

title: Suleiman opens national dialogue table at Baabda
why: Launched under the Doha Agreement to consolidate national reconciliation.

title: Lebanese Special Operations Command set up to group elite units
why: Set up from 2008 to group the army's elite units under one command.

title: Preacher Ahmad al-Assir arrested at Beirut airport on false passport
why: He had fled after the June 2013 Sidon clashes with the army.

title: Gebran Bassil chosen to lead Free Patriotic Movement
why: Succeeded Aoun as party leader before Aoun's 2016 presidency.

title: US Treasury sanctions Gebran Bassil
why: OFAC listed the FPM leader, President Aoun's son-in-law.

title: FPM announces cooperation with United Russia
why: Announced weeks after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

title: Cabinet declares Hezbollah's telecom network illegal and removes airport security chief
why: Called the network an attack on state sovereignty; Hezbollah's reaction led to the 7 May clashes.

title: Tripoli clashes erupt after Islamist Shadi Mawlawi's arrest
why: Fighting between Bab al-Tabbaneh and Jabal Mohsen killed nine over three days; the army deployed on 15 May.

title: Army deploys along Syria Street after three days of Tripoli fighting
why: Troops entered at about 6 am; nine had died, including a soldier hit by a sniper.

title: Hurriyyat Khassa created, early public LGBT rights group
why: Members began publicly organising for LGBT rights in 2002; Helem followed.

title: Meem founded to support LBTQ women
why: Lesbian, bisexual and trans women's group formed in August 2007.

title: Police raid Burj Hammoud cinema and test 36 men
why: Forced anal examinations drew a 'Tests of Shame' campaign; Justice Minister Qortbawi called for their end.

title: Dekwaneh mayor orders raid on gay-friendly nightclub
why: One of several local crackdowns on queer venues in the early 2010s.

title: Lebanese psychiatrists say homosexuality is not a disorder
why: Joint statements by the Psychiatric Society and LebMASH countered the pathologising used in prosecutions.

title: Morals bureau raids Beirut bathhouse, arrests 27 Syrians
why: Internal Security Forces raided a Turkish bathhouse in Beirut.

title: Beirut appeals court backs transgender man's right to change papers
why: Granted access to treatment; one of several court rulings softening Article 534.

title: LGBT activists stage sit-in outside Hbeish police station
why: About 50 people called for repeal of Article 534 of the Penal Code.

title: Mount Lebanon appeal court upholds acquittal of nine prosecuted over being gay
why: Reinforced the 2016 line that Article 534 does not cover consensual gay sex.
actors: Penal Appeal Court of Mount Lebanon

title: Military judge acquits four soldiers accused of sodomy
why: Judge Peter Germanos ruled in a landmark decision on Article 534.

title: Shura Council suspends interior minister's ban on LGBT gatherings
why: Suspended the directive Bassam Mawlawi issued in June 2022.
